title: Factorial ANOVA: interactions
biology: Beetle larvae from two genotypes are independently reared at two temperatures.
design: 22 independent larvae per genotype × temperature combination.
question: Does the temperature effect on mean growth depend on genotype?
null: The warm-minus-cool mean growth difference is the same for genotypes A and B.
options: genotype * heat includes both main effects and their interaction
The interaction coefficient is a difference of differences
Factor levels define the reference comparison
assumptions: Appropriate residual distribution and comparable residual spread
parametric: Model unequal residual spread if needed
Transform only when the transformed mean answers the question
nonparametric: A factorial permutation must preserve the design and tested term
Separate rank tests do not test the interaction
practice: Explain the interaction in words before reading its p-value.
code_simulate:
set.seed(2101)
d <- expand.grid(replicate = 1:22, genotype = c("A", "B"),
                 heat = c("Cool", "Warm"))
d$growth <- with(d, 14 + 1.4 * (genotype == "B") +
  2 * (heat == "Warm") + 2.3 * (genotype == "B" & heat == "Warm") +
  rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 2.1))
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
p <- ggplot(d, aes(heat, growth, color = genotype)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = .13,
    dodge.width = .35, seed = 21), alpha = .42, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point",
    position = position_dodge(.35), size = 4, shape = 18) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#246A73", "#B7663E")) +
  labs(x = "Rearing temperature", y = "Larval growth (mg/week)",
       color = "Genotype", caption = "Small points: individuals; diamonds: group means") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16)
print(p)
code_analysis:
fit <- lm(growth ~ genotype * heat, data = d)
summary(fit)
interaction_ci <- confint(fit)["genotypeB:heatWarm", ]
generating_model: There are 22 larvae in each of four genotype-by-temperature combinations. Growth = 14 + 1.4 if genotype B + 2 if warm + 2.3 if both genotype B and warm + independent Normal(0, 2.1²) error, in mg/week. Values are not rounded.
generating_truth: The temperature effect is 2 mg/week in genotype A and 4.3 mg/week in B, so the interaction is 2.3 mg/week. The interaction null is false.

columns.name: replicate
columns.meaning: Larva number within a genotype/temperature combination

teaching_point: An interaction is a difference of differences: a main-effect summary can conceal it.
